caption: The drawing consists of a large, detailed pewter or metal tankard with a hinged lid, ornate handle, and decorative elements, rendered in shades of grey pencil on a lightly yellowed background. The tankard is cylindrical with a wide, slightly flared base, and features a band of leaf-patterned trim around the bottom edge. Its main body is adorned with an elaborate crest or coat of arms surrounded by symmetrical scrollwork. The handle curves outward and upward, ending in a thumb piece with a scalloped edge and further decorative detailing where the handle attaches to the tankard. In the top left corner, a smaller, simplified sketch shows the tankard in side profile, emphasizing its proportions and lid mechanism. In the bottom right, there is a vertical detailed drawing of a column-like element, likely the tankard’s handle, featuring a sculpted lion’s head at the base, scrollwork, the engraved initials “H.B.S.”, and other ornamental features including a stylized dolphin motif. The entire composition is framed by a fine pencil border, and the artist’s signature, “Charles Cullen,” is inscribed at the bottom left. The drawing is monochromatic, relying on pencil shading to convey depth and highlights.
title: Silver Tankard
